claim_tested: Gtt3 has a GST-fold (thioredoxin-like N-terminal) domain
key_finding: 0 significant PDB100 hits full length (best prob 0.126, E=4.03); 0 hits for segments 1-239 and 130-245; AFDB-SwissProt returns self only; AFDB50 returns 14 fungal Gtt3 orthologues and no GST
context: S. cerevisiae AlphaFold model vs PDB100, AFDB-SwissProt, AFDB50
confidence: high; positive control in same run recovers GSTs for Gtt1 and Gtt2

claim_tested: The search protocol can detect GST folds when present
key_finding: AF-P40582 (Gtt1) 437 PDB100 hits, 344 titled glutathione/GST, prob 1.000, E 3.5e-13; AF-Q12390 (Gtt2) 578 hits, 451 titled glutathione/GST, top hit own structure 3ERF E 1.3e-31
context: Same Foldseek settings and database as the Gtt3 query
confidence: high; rules out a false negative from method insensitivity

claim_tested: Gtt3 contains the beta1-alpha1-beta2-beta3-beta4 thioredoxin sheet
key_finding: Gtt3 0 beta strands / 337 residues (53.7% helix). Controls: Gtt1 4, Gtt2 6, Ure2 4, Gto2 4, hGSTP1 4, hGSTA1 4, Grx1 4 strands
context: AlphaFold v6 models, identical code for all 8 proteins
confidence: high; structured regions of Gtt3 have pLDDT 90-96, so the absence is not low-confidence

claim_tested: Gtt3 has a catalytic Tyr/Ser/Cys at the GST G-site position
key_finding: No beta1 exists in Gtt3, so the beta1/alpha1 junction that carries the catalytic residue has no counterpart. Controls recover Gtt1 S14, Ure2 S121, Gto2 C46, Grx1 C27 (the known monothiol catalytic Cys) and hGSTP1 Tyr8 at the C-terminal end of beta1 (4-8)
confidence: high for the negative; the 8-residue window is a heuristic, exact G-site geometry needs superposition

claim_tested: Gtt3 carries a GST domain signature
key_finding: P39996 has only 6 signatures: PTHR41807/IPR038872 (1-337), PF27945/IPR060437 (11-68), PF30540/IPR063760 (165-335). No GST_N, GST_C, thioredoxin or glutaredoxin. GTT3_N and GTT3_C belong to no Pfam clan, while GST_N/GST_N_2/Glutaredoxin sit in CL0172 Thioredoxin and GST_C/GST_C_2 in CL0497
confidence: high; database-level, independent of this work's structure calls

claim_tested: Gtt3 is a degenerate GST that lost its G-site
key_finding: Across 70 of 1395 family members: SAP domain IPR003034 in 9 (12.9%), Rho-N/HeH IPR011112 in 1, Gtt3-specific domains in the rest. Zero members retain GST_N, GST_C, thioredoxin or glutaredoxin
confidence: medium-high; 70/1395 sample, but a degenerate GST family would be expected to retain signatures in some members

claim_tested: Gtt3 is detectably similar in sequence to GSTs
key_finding: Gtt3 vs Gtt1 Z=0.68, vs Gtt2 Z=-0.92, vs Gto2 Z=0.28, vs Ure2 Z=-0.07, vs hGSTP1 Z=-1.00 (all empirical p>0.2). Controls: Gtt2 vs hGSTP1 Z=11.3, Gtt1 vs Ure2 Z=4.78, Gtt1 vs Gtt2 Z=2.86
confidence: medium; pairwise SW is weak for remote homology (Gtt1 vs hGSTP1 also non-significant), so this is corroborative not decisive

claim_tested: Basis of the glutathione-metabolism assignment to YEL017W
key_finding: Network algorithm infers function from shared interaction partners; SGD cites this as the sole basis for 'may be involved in glutathione metabolism'
context: S. cerevisiae two-hybrid and AP-MS interaction data
confidence: high that this is the source; the inference itself is low-evidence guilt-by-association

claim_tested: Which yeast genes encode functional GSTs
key_finding: GTT1 and GTT2 identified and assayed as functional GSTs with CDNB; GTT3 not among them and never assayed
confidence: high for Gtt1/Gtt2; silent on Gtt3

claim_tested: Whether a further cellular GST remains after removing the known ones
key_finding: Grx1, Grx2, Gtt1 and Gtt2 account for the majority of cellular GST activity
confidence: medium; 'majority' leaves a residual, and a membrane protein may be missed in soluble extracts
